CFML Language Reference: Functions

DE

Returns its argument surrounded by double quotes, with any double quotes inside it doubled. The result is a string expression: when Evaluate or IIf evaluates it, you get the original text back instead of an attempt to look it up as a variable name.

Category

Dynamic evaluation functions

Syntax

DE(string)

Parameters

string
The string to protect from evaluation.

Returns

The string, enclosed in double quotes, with embedded double quotes escaped by doubling them.

Usage

DE stands for "delay evaluation". Its main customer is IIf, which evaluates whichever of its two string arguments it picks: IIf(x GT 0, DE("positive"), DE("negative")). Without DE, the word positive would be treated as a variable name and you would get an error.

DE does nothing useful on its own: it is only meaningful in front of Evaluate, IIf or SetVariable.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Quote = 'Andreessen said "Netscape everywhere"'>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Expression</TH><TH>Result</TH></TR>
<TR><TD>DE("Hello")</TD><TD>#DE("Hello")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>DE(Quote)</TD><TD>#HTMLEditFormat(DE(Quote))#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Evaluate(DE(Quote))</TD><TD>#HTMLEditFormat(Evaluate(DE(Quote)))#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>IIf(Year(Now()) GT 1999, DE("Y2K survived"), DE("Party!"))</TD>
    <TD>#IIf(Year(Now()) GT 1999, DE("Y2K survived"), DE("Party!"))#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>
